name: Office — core & shell
summary: Speculative multi-tenant office shell: structure, envelope, lobbies, core restrooms, vertical transportation and base-building MEP, plus on-site work; tenant improvements excluded (see office-ti). Cost is driven mainly by height/structure type, envelope (curtain wall vs. tilt-up/precast) and parking strategy. Data are good for Texas metros (Kirksey 2025) and gateway metros (Cumming, RLB); the national mid is a reasoned blend.

typicalSize.method: Judgment: suburban low/mid-rise spec office 2–6 floors; Kirksey mid/high-rise examples use 25,000-SF floor plates (e4) — 4 floors ≈ 100,000 SF.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Derived: at 4 spaces/1,000 SF (e11) × ≈350 SF/space incl. aisles = 1,400 SF of parking per 1,000 SF office; a 3-story building at 50% site coverage for building+parking+landscape gives ≈ 13,000–17,000 GSF/acre. Mid-rise with a garage reaches ≈25,000.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Spaces per GSF: Kirksey assumes 4/1,000 (low-rise) and 5/1,000 (flex); urban/mid-rise projects with garages often 3/1,000.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Baseline = speculative low/mid-rise (2–6 story) core & shell incl. typical surface-parked sitework, standard quality. Direct scope matches: Kirksey 2025 low-rise Houston $115–139 (e1), Austin $133–161 (e3), Dallas $190–235 (e2); mid-rise Dallas $225–280 (e4). Average of the three Texas low-rise midpoints ≈ $171; Texas metros price below national, so national ≈ $190–200. Cross-check: RSMeans 2026 complete 2–4 story office $253.63 (e8) less ≈9% A/E fee and ≈20% basic interiors ≈ $185, plus ≈$20–25 sitework ≈ $205–210. Mid = $210. Low = $140 ≈ Houston/Austin low-rise (cheapest open-shop suburban shells). High = $360 = Cumming 10-metro median low for urban shell & core excl. sitework (e5); prime high-rise in gateway metros exceeds this (RLB prime median $357–588, e6). RSMeans 2019/2022 whole-building figures (e7, e9) are kept as evidence but not used directly because they include interiors and are older dollars.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. general conditions and OH&P for site + core & shell (warm lit shell to tenant demising, no TI). Excludes land, soft costs, TI, structured parking, off-sites, impact/tap fees.

qualityTiers.method: economy ≈ low/mid (140/210 ≈ 0.67, rounded up to 0.75 for small-building premium); premium ≈ Cumming urban shell & core mid ($405) / 300 region-adjusted ≈ 1.35; luxury ≈ RLB prime-office median midpoint ($472) / 270 ≈ 1.75.

systemSplit.method: Derived. Sitework (31+32+33) = 14% from Kirksey: sitework $14–20 of $115–139 (≈13–14%, e1) and $21–33 of $190–235 (≈11–14%, e2). MEP shares scaled down from RSMeans whole-office medians (plumbing 3.78%, mechanical 8.2%, electrical 10%, e9) because core & shell carries base-building MEP only. Remaining building shell split by typical steel-frame/precast-or-glass spec office proportions (judgment): structure (03+05) 24%, envelope (07+08) 20%, GC/fee 9%, elevators 3%, core/lobby finishes 4%.

lineItems.name: On-site work incl. surface parking (carve-out)

cost.method: Kirksey 2025 low-rise sitework per GSF: Houston $14–20, Austin $20–27, Dallas $21–33. Mid ≈ average of midpoints (17, 23.5, 27) ≈ $22.

lineItems.notes: Already inside the baseline; shown so users can see the site share.

lineItems.name: Structured parking garage (above grade)

cost.method: Cumming Q4 2025 above-grade garage per stall: Nashville $24k–41k, Dallas $26k–45k, Boston $34k–59k. Mid ≈ Dallas/Nashville midpoint average (≈$34k) rounded. Kirksey Dallas 2025 garages $62–125/SF ≈ $21k–41k/stall at 330 SF/stall (same order).

lineItems.notes: Turn on for mid-rise/urban sites; qty default 3 spaces per 1,000 GSF.

lineItems.name: Passenger elevators (hydraulic, low-rise)
lineItems.notes: Inside baseline; use traction (≈$250k each, building-systems block) above ~5 floors.

pctOfHard.method: Derived. A/E 6–7% (RSMeans office models, e13) + permits/inspections 1–2% + survey/geotech/testing 1% + legal/insurance/taxes during construction 2–3% + developer fee 3–5% + leasing/marketing of spec space 3–5% + owner's rep/PM 1–2%. Financing excluded. | Second pass (2026-10-24, main session): Reduced 4 points to remove the developer fee (3–5%). The engine adds impact & tap fees, the developer fee and construction financing as their own lines (docs/BUDGET_ENGINE.md §5), so this bucket must exclude them.

softCosts.notes: Leasing commissions for speculative office can add 4–8% of hard cost if included in the budget; tenant improvement allowances belong to office-ti.

design.method: Industry norm for conceptual budgets: 5% at schematic, falling to ~2–3% by CDs.

hard.method: Typical owner hard-cost contingency for new ground-up commercial shell work.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard low ($140) × (1 + 0.18 soft) ≈ $165 rounded down for rural tilt-up; max ≈ Cumming urban shell & core high ($520 NYC, e5) × 1.15 soft ≈ $600.

openQuestions: No public national core-&-shell-only benchmark was found; national mid is inferred from Texas (Kirksey) and gateway-metro (Cumming, RLB) data.
RLB office figures do not state whether they are shell-only or fitted-out — confirm with RLB notes.
Kirksey Dallas 2025 low-rise ($190–235) is ~50% above Houston ($115–139) for the same building description; worth confirming.
